bills.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
bills.status: Passed Senate with an amendment and an amendment to the Title by Yea-Nay Vote. 90 - 6. Record Vote Number: 228.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6500 directly affects Treasury's budget authority and appropriations for FY2027, including funding levels for IRS, FinCEN, OFR, and Departmental Offices. Treasury's Office of Legislative Affairs and the Office of Management and Budget liaison must track the Senate amendment closely, as any rider or funding limitation could restrict operational capacity or create a continuing resolution compliance burden across Treasury bureaus.

bills.title: Digital Asset Market Clarity Act
bills.status: Cloture motion on the motion to proceed to the measure presented in Senate.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3633 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Terrorism and Financial Intelligence and FinCEN, as the bill reallocates regulatory jurisdiction over digital assets between the SEC and CFTC while preserving or potentially reshaping existing Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering obligations for digital asset intermediaries. Treasury's implementation risk centers on ensuring that any jurisdictional handoff does not create regulatory gaps in AML/KYC coverage or undermine OFAC's sanctions compliance expectations for digital asset platforms.

bills.title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
bills.status: Passed Senate with an amendment and an amendment to the Title by Yea-Nay Vote. 86 - 11. Record Vote Number: 224.
bills.nexus: Without a known nexus or bill text provided, I cannot responsibly characterize which specific Treasury office or authority H.R. 5334 touches or its precise implementation risk. Please supply the bill text or a summary so the brief is accurate and actionable.

bills.title: Common Cents Act
bills.status: Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
bills.nexus: The Common Cents Act, which would eliminate the penny and direct Treasury to round cash transactions to the nearest nickel, directly implicates the Bureau of Engraving and Printing and the U.S. Mint under Treasury's coinage and currency production authorities. Treasury's implementation risk centers on managing the wind-down of penny production, updating seigniorage accounting, and coordinating with the Federal Reserve on coin circulation transition.

bills.title: A bill to expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.
bills.status: Passed Senate with an amendment by Unanimous Consent.
bills.nexus: S. 2677 directly implicates Treasury through U.S. Customs and Border Protection, which sits within DHS but coordinates closely with Treasury on trade enforcement and revenue collection at the border. The bill's expansion of information-sharing authorities for suspected IP violations creates implementation questions around data-handling protocols, interagency coordination agreements, and potential liability exposure for CBP trade enforcement operations.

bills.title: Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act
bills.status: Passed Senate without amendment by Unanimous Consent.
bills.nexus: H.R. 5366 directly implicates IRS and the Office of Tax Policy by excluding certain federal disaster relief payments from gross income under the Internal Revenue Code. Treasury's implementation risk centers on revenue scoring, guidance issuance, and ensuring consistent IRS administration of the exclusion across multiple declared disaster areas.

bills.title: A bill to amend title 10, United States Code, to eliminate the recoupment of separation pay, special separation benefits, and voluntary separation incentive payments from members of the Armed Forces who subsequently receive disability compensation under laws administered by the Department of Veterans Affairs and to impose limitations on the authority of the Secretary of Defense to recoup such pay from members who subsequently receive military retired or retainer pay.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
bills.nexus: S. 5367 touches DoD's military personnel accounts and the statutory offset mechanism that currently flows recouped funds back to the Treasury, implicating Treasury's interest in any legislative change to federal intragovernmental offsets and mandatory spending. The bill's elimination or limitation of recoupment creates a direct revenue loss risk to the general fund and may require OMB score coordination with Treasury on the mandatory spending baseline.

bills.title: A resolution expressing support for the designation of the first week of August 2026, as "National Community Health Center Week", encouraging all people of the United States to participate by visiting their local community health center, and celebrating the important partnership between community health centers and the communities they serve.
bills.status: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent.
bills.nexus: S.Res. 843 is a simple sense-of-the-Senate resolution with no appropriations, tax, or financial regulatory provisions, giving Treasury no jurisdictional hook through any of its offices or bureaus. There is no implementation burden or fiscal risk for Treasury to track.

bills.title: A bill to reauthorize and expand the imposition of sanctions under the Nicaragua Investment Conditionality Act of 2018, and for other purposes.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because the Nicaragua Investment Conditionality Act (NICA Act) directs the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to administer and enforce economic sanctions against Nicaraguan government officials and entities. Reauthorization and expansion would require OFAC to update its Specially Designated Nationals list, revise existing general licenses, and absorb increased compliance and enforcement workload tied to any new designations or sectoral restrictions.

bills.title: A bill to require the Secretary of the Army to issue guidance relating to the review of applications for alteration or temporary or permanent occupation or use of certain hydropower projects, and for other purposes.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
bills.nexus: S. 4992 directs the Army Corps of Engineers on permitting procedures for hydropower projects, which does not directly implicate Treasury's statutory authorities, appropriations, or tax expenditures. Treasury should monitor it only if hydropower project financing involves tax-exempt bonds or energy tax credits administered by IRS, where regulatory delays could affect credit utilization timelines or bond compliance.

bills.title: Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 4297 would restrict the use of federal funds for private-school voucher programs, directly implicating Treasury's role in administering tax-expenditure provisions and any bond-financed public-school funding structures under IRS authority. The Finance Committee referral signals likely tax-code amendments, raising implementation risk for IRS guidance and potential revenue-scoring obligations for Treasury's Office of Tax Policy.

bills.title: Credit Card Competition Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: S. 3623 would amend the Electronic Fund Transfer Act to require credit card network routing competition, directly implicating the Office of Domestic Finance and its oversight of payment system regulation under Treasury's statutory role in financial market infrastructure policy. Treasury's implementation concern centers on potential disruption to interchange fee structures and network security standards, which could affect systemic risk in consumer payment markets and require coordinated rulemaking with the Federal Reserve and OCC.

bills.title: CREATE Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: The CREATE Act falls within Treasury's jurisdiction because it involves tax incentives or credits administered by IRS, touching the Office of Tax Policy's authority to evaluate revenue impact and regulatory design. Treasury's implementation risk centers on IRS capacity to administer new credit provisions accurately and the potential for compliance complexity or revenue loss if eligibility rules are poorly defined.

bills.title: America's Olympic and Paralympic Games Commemorative Coins Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs. (Sponsor introductory remarks on measure: CR S4337-4338)
bills.nexus: S. 2265 authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue commemorative coins for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games, directly implicating the U.S. Mint (a Treasury bureau) and its coin production and surcharge distribution authorities under 31 U.S.C. Chapter 51. Treasury's implementation risk centers on coordinating mintage limits, pricing, and surcharge payments to designated beneficiaries while managing working capital and production schedules within the Mint's Public Enterprise Fund.

bills.title: Buying American Cotton Act of 2025
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 1919 falls within Treasury's purview because domestic-content mandates tied to federal procurement or tax incentives would engage the Office of Tax Policy and potentially require IRS guidance or rulemaking. The implementation risk centers on whether any tax credit or penalty mechanism in the bill creates administrative burden, revenue impact, or interaction with existing trade-related tax provisions that Treasury must score and operationalize.

bills.title: 25th Anniversary of 9/11 Commemorative Coin Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because commemorative coin legislation falls under the authority of the United States Mint, a Treasury bureau responsible for designing, producing, and issuing such coins under 31 U.S.C. Chapter 51. The implementation angle centers on Mint resource planning, surcharge disbursement oversight, and ensuring the program does not draw on appropriated funds, consistent with the self-liquidating model required by law.

bills.title: HELPER Act of 2025
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: The HELPER Act targets homeownership assistance for teachers, law enforcement, and other public servants, likely through FHA mortgage insurance modifications or down-payment programs that fall under Treasury's housing finance and tax-expenditure equities. Treasury cares because any FHA credit subsidy costs must be scored against the federal budget, and preferential mortgage terms could interact with existing tax provisions such as the mortgage interest deduction, requiring OTP and OGC review for fiscal and legal consistency.

bills.title: TAILOR Act of 2025
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
bills.nexus: The TAILOR Act would require federal financial regulators, including OFR and potentially FSOC's member agencies under Treasury's purview, to tailor rules to the size and risk profile of regulated institutions. Treasury cares because overly rigid implementation could constrain the office's ability to calibrate systemic-risk oversight and could create compliance asymmetries that affect financial stability monitoring.
